subject: 🏃 Thursday — 6 mi Steady Base (Wk 1)
html:
Tomorrow: 6 mi Steady Base — 8:30–8:45 pace

Day after your first heavy strength session, so expect the legs to feel a bit thick early. That's normal — the pace target is deliberately moderate. Run the first mile at 8:45–9:00 and let the legs come to you. If they don't loosen up by mile 2, hold 8:45 for the full run and call it a win.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Hip CARs (3 each direction, each leg) → banded lateral walks (10 each direction) → glute bridges (10 reps, 2-sec hold at top) → quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side).

The run: 6 miles at 8:30–8:45/mi. Flat route preferred — Bayfront or Sawyer Camp out-and-back. HR should sit 140–150; if it's creeping above 155 at 8:45 pace, you're still fatigued from the gym — slow down rather than chase the number.

Focus cue: Cadence. After Tuesday's track session and today's squats, your stride will want to shorten and shuffle. Actively think about quick, light turnover — aim for 170+ spm. Quick feet protect the knee better than long strides.

Context: Week 1 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation & Durability — 80 days to race day. Knee has been a clean 1/5 through every session this block, including Tuesday's 8.4-mile track day (max HR 190). Four straight 1/5 readings is exactly the signal we needed to trust the ramp. Keep reporting honestly — this data is what lets us push when we should and back off when we must.

Prep tonight: Lay out your run kit. Coffee + a banana or toast 30 min before is enough for 6 easy miles. Get to bed by 10 — you've stacked a track day and a heavy lift in 48 hours, and sleep is where the adaptation actually happens.
